finding: `thinking: Some(ThinkingConfig::disabled())` is NOT inert: gemini.rs emits `thinkingConfig{thinkingBudget:0}` for ANY Some(thinking), which models that cannot disable thinking reject with a 400 -> soft-swallowed -> every conversation untitled. The exact bug being fixed, reintroduced for another provider. (Anthropic's Disabled arm is an empty branch, so the comment was wrong about it too.)

`query_terms` split only on whitespace while the corpus is normalized on punctuation/camelCase, so a term like `project,` matched nothing and — under the ALL-terms rule — emptied the whole result. Same failure class as the bug being fixed, one keystroke away.

Strict ALL-terms with no fallback still returns 0 for natural sentences a model actually writes (`please create a new project`, `turn off memory retrieval` measured against the real 446-op catalog) — including the phrasing the new MemorySettings e2e uses.

The approval assertions could not fail: a fresh conversation defaults to manual_approve (migration + ApprovalMode::default), so the card appears for EVERY tool. Deleting the control force-approval branch entirely would leave TEST-14/15/16 and the Rust real_llm_write_requires_approval all green. INV-4 was asserted by a tautology.

TEST-18 claimed 'the chat reflects it' but asserted only that an `invoke_capability` tool-call ROW exists — strictly implied by the preceding project-count assertion, so it added zero discriminating power and nothing inspected the transcript.

`listJson` returned [] on any non-OK response, so every NEGATIVE assertion (deny -> nothing created, restricted user -> no project) was satisfied by a 401/403/500 on the verification GET. The proofs were unfalsifiable.

TEST-17(a) passed vacuously if the restricted user could not reach /api/control/mcp at all (operationIds returns [] on an error body, and the describe assertion accepts ANY error including the control::use rejection). No assertion proved the filter RAN and merely excluded the op.

TEST-17(b) approved only `if (await approve.isVisible(...))` and asserted nothing about the invoke being attempted, so a model that never reached the mutating call produced a green run that never touched the authorization gate.

The unit tests' `ranked()` helper retyped the production filter+comparator, so TEST-1/2/3 proved the ranking of a COPY: dropping the tie-break or inverting the comparator in `list_capabilities` left them green.

`resolve_test_llm` treated the committed `sk-xxx` placeholder in tests/.env.test as a configured LLM, so a stock box drives a paid SaaS endpoint with a garbage key — and the placeholder OPENAI_API_KEY shadowed a genuinely-exported real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

Both seams enumerated only OpenAI+Anthropic while the repo's own get_or_create_ai_provider (and provider-helpers.ts) support Gemini+Groq, so a Gemini/Groq box went dark while the skip message claimed 'no LLM configured at all' — the same failure the feature exists to end, narrower.

The anti-regression guard was line-scoped and non-recursive, so a prettier line-wrap, a hoisted `const HAS_X = process.env...`, or a spec in a subdirectory evaded it entirely — the exact shape the pre-fix spec used.
TEST-17(a) is pure JSON-RPC + REST and needs no model, yet sat behind the LLM skip gate — an authorization proof going dark on an LLM-less box, a small instance of the failure mode being fixed.
The design's matrix says 'for each: ... deny -> nothing created'. The settings operation class had an approve leg but no deny leg.

The vendor table was a 5-tuple array plus a PARALLEL defaults array, so adding a vendor took three edits and a drift between them produced `model_name: ""` via unwrap_or_default() — failing far downstream instead of at the seam.

`TestLlm` dropped the env var it resolved from, so two call sites re-derived it as format!("{}_API_KEY", provider_type.to_uppercase()) — an inference that breaks for any vendor naming its key otherwise.
`should_retry_with_larger_budget`'s `title` parameter was dead on the production path (the caller passed a literal None after an early return), so half its unit cases guarded unreachable behavior.

`prior_title_requests` was counted and the request pushed under SEPARATE lock acquisitions, so two concurrent title calls against one stub both observe prior==0 and both take the 'first call fails' branch — and the new budget_once mode depends on that count being exact.
`term_score` recomputed `id_segments`/`summary_words` (allocating Vec<String>) for every (operation x term) pair over a 446-op catalog, and the term count was unbounded.

A zero-result `list_capabilities` said only '0 operation(s) you can run:' — no statement of the matching rule and no retry guidance, which is exactly what left the live model repeating the same call and then flailing.

The model-facing `query` tool description still describes the pre-fix semantics ('free-text filter matched against operation_id, summary and tags') and does not mention the all-terms rule or relevance ordering.

~30 other real-LLM Rust tests across 16 files still gate on `env::var("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")`, so they keep reporting SKIPPED on an OpenAI-bridge box. The new rule is adopted only for the control tier + the title test.

`createToolCapableModel` is a near-copy of agent-llm-helpers.ts::createBridgeToolModel (differing only in maxTokens/context_length/model source); the Rust seam likewise re-implements rather than delegates to the sibling `test_provider_base_url`.
The search matcher reads only catalog-owned fields and arguably belongs in sdk/crates/ziee-control-mcp beside `Operation`, not app-side in handlers.rs.

The escalated retry is a SECOND untimed generation on the awaited turn-end path, so the worst case adds a 4096- plus an 8192-token generation between the assistant's last token and the turn completing.

For `delete user` the ASCII tie-break puts LitSearch.deleteUserKey / LlmProvider.deleteUserApiKey above User.delete (all score 16), so 'the operation the phrase names comes first' does not hold universally.

No isolation defect: testInfra is a per-test fixture with a fresh database and worker-locked ports, resolve_test_llm takes an injected lookup (no process-env mutation), TEST_LLM is a read-only module const, and per-test server env goes through TestServerOptions.extra_env.
No OpenAPI regen required: no JsonSchema type, route, handler signature, permission or SyncEntity is touched, and list_capabilities' {operations,returned,total,truncated} keys are byte-identical.

Every new production symbol has a live caller (matcher -> list_capabilities; retry/budget symbols -> generate_title_with_ai; stub modes -> stub_chat + title_test; both seams -> the real-LLM tests and the specs). No dead-but-tested code.
